source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-11), the stick seen from behind-left (pilot's view) and above, head buttons toward the camera, palm rest to the right
mappingSource: catalog (thrustmaster.json, confidence low: "which button number sits where is not documented -> buttons without input"; axes Rz twist, Z throttle, X/Y per the FlightGear map). The FlightGear Fox 2 Pro USB map comments (https://gitlab.com/flightgear/fgdata/-/blob/next/Input/Joysticks/ThrustMaster/Top-Gun-Fox2-Pro-USB.xml) do say where each button is (0-based): 0 trigger, 1 yellow/black button, 2 side button above the trigger, 3 right button next to the yellow/black one, 4 outside bottom, 5 middle bottom, 6 inside bottom; Thrustmaster's support page has no manual
note: The three "Head button" parts are interchangeable in the catalog (no input numbers): thumb.1 = yellow/black button (FlightGear 1 -> Windows button 2), thumb.2 = right wedge (FlightGear 3 -> button 4), thumb.3 = side button above the trigger (FlightGear 2 -> button 3), assigned by JoyPro only. The catalog could take these numbers from the FlightGear comments. The base buttons and the throttle slider are not identifiable for certain: three dark recesses sit under the orange/white scale at the base front (likely the three "bottom" buttons, kept as hidden candidates); the throttle slider is not identified on this photo. Caution: the orange-to-white scale with the recesses under it may instead be the throttle slider running in an arc slot (the scale reads like a throttle gauge), so a reviewer should check a real device or another photo before showing any of these.
